scripts.title: Stop and disable a Windows service
scripts.intent: Stop a running service and set its startup type to Disabled. Use when a persistence audit flags a service running from a user-writable path or with a generic display name. Reversible via Set-Service if a mistake.

service_name.description: Service short name (not display name). Validated against the standard Windows service-name character set.

scripts.title: Re-enable and start a Windows service
scripts.intent: Set a service's startup type (default Automatic) and start it. Use to undo a mistaken host-stop-service, or to bring a legitimate vendor service back online after triage clears it. Refuses missing services. Reversible via host-stop-service.

service_name.description: Service short name (not display name). Validated against the standard Windows service-name character set.

startup_type.description: Startup type to set before starting. Automatic for services that should run at boot; Manual for on-demand services.

scripts.title: Remove a Windows scheduled task
scripts.intent: Unregister a scheduled task by its full path. Use when a persistence audit flags a task with a non-vendor principal or an action pointing at a user-writable path. Irreversible without re-creating the task; the operator should capture the action / trigger first if forensic preservation is needed.

task_path.description: Full task path including leading backslash, e.g. \UpdaterX or \Microsoft\Windows\Foo\Bar.

scripts.title: Remove a Windows autorun registry value
scripts.intent: Delete a value from HKLM or HKCU Run / RunOnce. Use when a persistence audit flags a non-vendor entry. Reversible via reg add if mistake; the operator should record the value data before removal if forensic preservation is needed.

scripts.title: Remove an Image File Execution Options hijack (T1546.012)
scripts.intent: Per-image IFEO + SilentProcessExit cleanup. Use when a RegistryPersistEdit / T1546.012 detection identifies an attacker-set Debugger or MonitorProcess on `<victim.exe>`. Walks both 64-bit and 32-bit (Wow6432Node) IFEO and SilentProcessExit subkeys for the supplied image; removes Debugger / MonitorProcess / ReportingMode unconditionally and removes GlobalFlag only when the silent-exit trigger bit (0x200) is set (Microsoft uses GlobalFlag legitimately on system processes -- wholesale removal is unsafe). Sweeps the empty subkey afterward. Refuses system-critical binaries (cmd.exe, explorer.exe, svchost.exe, lsass.exe, etc.) -- a bad revert there can lock out remote response mid-IR; remediate those by hand after confirming alternate access. Reversible by re-creating the value with reg add if forensic preservation matters; capture the prior value from the script's audit lines before approving the live run.

image_name.description: Image filename (basename only, e.g. `sethc.exe`, `osk.exe`, `notepad.exe`). Not a full path -- IFEO keys are indexed by basename. Must include an extension.

scripts.title: Set or revert a security-hardening registry value
scripts.intent: Slot-driven primitive for credential-theft / lateral-movement registry hardening. The script ships a curated catalog of well-understood targets (WDigest UseLogonCredential, LSA RunAsPPL / NoLMHash / LmCompatibilityLevel / DisableRestrictedAdmin, Winlogon AutoAdminLogon / DefaultPassword, PrintNightmare Point-and-Print). Each slot encodes hive + key path + value name + type + the hardened 'green' default + an allowed-values whitelist. Omit `value` to revert to the slot's green default (the common case after a persistence audit flags a weakened key). Supply `value` to write an explicit allowed value (e.g. RunAsPPL=2 for UEFI lock). Some slots delete rather than set (DefaultPassword). Reversible by re-running with the original `value`. Refuses unknown slots and out-of-list values. Adding a new finding = adding a row to the catalog -- do not use this primitive for arbitrary registry edits, build a finding-specific cleanup script for those.

slot.description: Curated hardening target. Each slot encodes the registry coordinates and a green default. See the script body for hive/path/value-name + the why.

value.description: Explicit value to write. Must be in the slot's allowed-values list (DWord slots take a numeric string; String slots take the literal). Omit to revert to the slot's hardened green default.

scripts.title: Delete a file from disk
scripts.intent: Remove a single file by absolute path. Use when a detection or persistence audit surfaces a malicious binary or script in a user-writable location and the operator has decided to evict it. Refuses to touch C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, C:\Program Files (x86), or C:\ProgramData\Microsoft. Pair with host-kill-process if the file is currently mapped by a running process. Irreversible — capture forensic copy first if needed.

path.description: Absolute Windows file path, e.g. C:\Users\bob\AppData\Local\Temp\foo.exe. Drive-letter rooted; system directories are blocked at runtime.

scripts.title: Delete a folder and its contents recursively
scripts.intent: Recursively remove a directory tree. Use when a detection or persistence audit identifies a malicious staging folder (e.g. C:\Users\<u>\AppData\Local\Temp\<campaign-name>) and the operator has decided to evict the entire tree. Refuses C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, C:\Program Files (x86), C:\ProgramData\Microsoft (including subtrees) and bare C:\Users, C:\Users\Public, C:\ProgramData. Refuses paths shallower than 3 segments. Reports file count + total bytes before deletion. Pair with host-kill-process if any binary in the tree is currently mapped by a running process.

path.description: Absolute Windows folder path. Drive-letter rooted; minimum 3 segments enforced at runtime; system trees blocked at runtime.

scripts.title: Quarantine a file (forensics-preserving)
scripts.intent: Move a file to C:\ProgramData\FalconCleanup\quarantine with restricted ACL (SYSTEM + Administrators only) and write a sidecar manifest recording original path, size, mtime, and SHA-256 prefix. Use INSTEAD OF host-delete-file when forensic preservation matters (active investigation, regulated environment, ambiguous true-positive). Same protected-directory block-list as host-delete-file. Reversible by moving the .quarantined file back to its original path; refer to the .manifest.json sidecar.

path.description: Absolute Windows file path. Drive-letter rooted; system directories are blocked at runtime.

scripts.title: Enumerate WMI event-subscription persistence (read-only)
scripts.intent: List every __EventFilter, __FilterToConsumerBinding, and EventConsumer in root\subscription on the host, cross-link them into chains (filter → binding → consumer), and flag suspicious entries via heuristics: __InstanceModificationEvent timer queries (T1546.003), CommandLineEventConsumer invoking interpreters / lolbins / encoded commands, ActiveScriptEventConsumer (rare and attacker-favored), random-looking filter names. Microsoft-shipped defaults (SCM Event Log Filter, BVTConsumer) are excluded from the suspicious flag. Output is a JSON document with `chains[]`, `orphan_consumers[]`, `orphan_bindings[]`, and `suspicious_filter_names[]` — feed each entry in `suspicious_filter_names` to `host-remove-wmi-persistence` as the `filter_name` param. Use in IR Phase 0 — WMI persistence is invisible to the RegistryKey audit and the autorun sweep, so this is the only enumeration that catches it. The script is read-only (Get-CimInstance only) but routes through the gated cleanup channel; one approval per IR run is the cost.

scripts.title: Remove a WMI event-subscription persistence chain
scripts.intent: Delete the WMI persistence triple (__EventFilter + __FilterToConsumerBinding + __EventConsumer) in root\subscription matching a given filter name. WMI subscriptions are a common attacker-persistence vector that the RegistryKey audit cannot see. Operator must supply the exact filter Name — get this from a Sysmon Event ID 19/20/21 detection or from a manual `Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\subscription -ClassName __EventFilter` review. Irreversible; capture the Query / CommandLineTemplate beforehand if forensic preservation is needed.

filter_name.description: Exact Name property of the __EventFilter to remove. Bindings and consumers referenced by this filter are also removed.

scripts.title: Disable a local user account
scripts.intent: Disable a local Windows account via Disable-LocalUser. Use when a credential-compromise detection or persistence audit identifies an attacker-created or attacker-controlled account. Refuses Administrator, DefaultAccount, Guest, WDAGUtilityAccount, SYSTEM. Reversible via Enable-LocalUser. Domain accounts are out of scope — use AD tooling for those.

username.description: Local account short name (not display name).

scripts.title: Enable a local user account
scripts.intent: Re-enable a local Windows account via Enable-LocalUser. Use to undo a mistaken host-disable-local-user, or to restore a legitimate account after triage clears it. Refuses DefaultAccount, Guest, WDAGUtilityAccount, SYSTEM (Administrator is allowed since re-enabling the built-in admin can be deliberate). Refuses missing accounts. Reversible via host-disable-local-user. Domain accounts are out of scope.

username.description: Local account short name (not display name).

scripts.title: Force logoff an interactive user session
scripts.intent: Terminate any active interactive session(s) for a given username via quser + logoff. Use during credential-compromise IR to evict an attacker's live session before they react. Refuses SYSTEM, NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SERVICE, DWM*, UMFD*. Pair with host-disable-local-user to prevent immediate re-login. Disruptive to legitimate work in flight — only run after the operator has confirmed the user / host pairing is hostile.

username.description: Username whose interactive sessions will be logged off.

scripts.title: Block outbound traffic to a remote IP via Windows Firewall
scripts.intent: Create a Windows Firewall outbound block rule (New-NetFirewallRule, Profile=Any, Enabled=True) for a single remote IPv4 address. Use to cut a host's connection to a known C2 IP without full network containment — useful when you want telemetry to keep flowing while severing the malicious channel. Refuses RFC1918 / loopback / link-local / 0.0.0.0 / 255.x ranges. Reversible via Remove-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'FalconCleanup-Block-<ip>'. Note: per-host firewall rules don't propagate across the fleet; for fleet-wide blocking use a Falcon Firewall Management policy or contain the host instead.

remote_ip.description: IPv4 address to block outbound traffic toward.

scripts.title: Stop and fully delete a Windows service
scripts.intent: Stop the service, then sc.exe delete it (full removal of the service-control-manager registration). Use INSTEAD OF host-stop-service when the operator wants the service gone, not just disabled — typical after persistence-audit confirms the service is attacker-installed. Irreversible without re-creating the service; pair with host-delete-file or host-delete-folder to also remove the binary. The earlier host-stop-service is preferable when the entry might be benign-but-suspicious and you want a reversible action.

scripts.title: Kill a running process
scripts.intent: Force-stop a process by PID or by image-name regex. Use to clear an actively-running malicious process discovered during triage. Process may respawn if a parent service or scheduled task is still in place — pair with host-stop-service or host-remove-scheduled-task as appropriate.

pid.description: Numeric PID. Either pid or image_name must be supplied; pid wins if both.

image_name.description: Process image name (without .exe), matched as a substring against Get-Process .ProcessName.

scripts.title: Uninstall an AppX/MSIX package (generic Store-package eviction)
scripts.intent: Generic eviction primitive for AppX/MSIX packages that don't have a dedicated cleanup script. Use when an IR or Shadow-AI finding identifies a Store package by name and the package is in C:\Program Files\WindowsApps (which host-delete-folder refuses by design — that path is system-protected and Remove-AppxPackage is the only correct cleanup). Calls Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers + Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers per match, then Get-AppxProvisionedPackage + Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage so the package doesn't auto-install for new users on next logon. Bundled services (CoworkVMService et al. registered by the MSIX) are removed alongside the package. Refuses well-known Microsoft system packages (Edge, WebView2, AppInstaller, StorePurchaseApp, the Windows shell stack) and the bare-wildcard pattern. Match pattern supports Get-AppxPackage's -Name wildcard syntax.

package_name_pattern.description: Get-AppxPackage -Name pattern. Supports `*` wildcard. Example: `Claude` matches Claude_<ver>_<arch>__<publisher>; `*Cursor*` matches any package whose family name contains Cursor.

scripts.title: Uninstall AnyDesk (RMM-persistence removal)
scripts.intent: Evict AnyDesk end-to-end: stop and sc.exe delete the AnyDesk service, kill any running AnyDesk.exe (covers the portable variant attackers drop in %APPDATA% / %ProgramData%), invoke the vendor uninstaller (`AnyDesk.exe --remove --silent`) from each known install root, and sweep the install + config directories. Use when a persistence audit or detection identifies AnyDesk as attacker-deployed remote-access tooling (BlackByte, Akira, BlackCat, Conti spinoffs all favor it). Irreversible. Refuse if IT has legitimately deployed AnyDesk for support — confirm with the operator before running. Config sweep is intentional: leftover settings carry the install id attackers reuse to re-authenticate.

scripts.title: Uninstall Cursor (Shadow-AI eviction)
scripts.intent: Evict Cursor end-to-end: kill running Cursor processes (Squirrel main + Electron renderer children), invoke the Squirrel uninstaller from every per-user install root (DisplayName 'Cursor' / 'Cursor (User)'), and sweep per-profile install + cache + MCP-config dirs (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\cursor, %APPDATA%\Cursor\User\globalStorage, Cache, Code Cache). Walks every user profile under SYSTEM context — Cursor is per-user Squirrel, not system-wide MSI. Project-level ~/.cursor settings intentionally preserved so re-sanctioning later restores workspace settings. Pair with extras_host_group_action(action='add-hosts', group_id=$FALCON_SHADOW_AI_BANNED_GROUP_ID) to attach the prevention policy. Irreversible. Confirm with operator that Cursor is not corp-deployed before running.

scripts.title: Uninstall Ollama (Shadow-AI eviction)
scripts.intent: Evict Ollama end-to-end: stop+delete the Ollama service (recent versions), kill tray app + daemon + ollama_llama_server children, invoke the Inno Setup uninstaller (DisplayName 'Ollama' / 'Ollama for Windows', /SILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART), sweep install roots across every user profile, and remove the per-user Run-key autostart. Sweep includes %USERPROFILE%\.ollama (model store, multi-GB) — main data-egress surface; preserved models would let a re-installed Ollama re-expose them without operator review. Ollama exposes a local OpenAI-compatible REST API on 11434; service teardown + process kill severs it. Pair with extras_host_group_action(add-hosts) to attach the AI prevention policy. Irreversible.

scripts.title: Uninstall LM Studio (Shadow-AI eviction)
scripts.intent: Evict LM Studio end-to-end: kill running LM Studio processes (Squirrel main + helper), invoke the Squirrel uninstaller (DisplayName 'LM Studio'), sweep per-profile install roots (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LM Studio, %APPDATA%\LM Studio) and the model cache (%USERPROFILE%\.cache\lm-studio, ~\.lmstudio). LM Studio exposes an OpenAI-compatible local server on 1234 by default; process kill severs it (no service). Model cache sweep is intentional for the same data-egress reason as Ollama. Pair with extras_host_group_action(add-hosts) to attach the AI prevention policy. Irreversible.

scripts.title: Uninstall Claude Desktop (Shadow-AI eviction)
scripts.intent: Evict Claude Desktop (Anthropic) end-to-end: PRESERVE %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json by renaming to .quarantined-<timestamp> BEFORE any sweep (forensic preservation of MCP-server registrations the user wired up), kill running Claude processes, invoke the Squirrel uninstaller (DisplayName 'Claude' / 'Claude Desktop'), sweep per-profile install + cache dirs (%LOCALAPPDATA%\AnthropicClaude, %APPDATA%\Claude\Cache + Code Cache + GPUCache). Claude Desktop's MCP-host capability is the load-bearing concern — registered MCP servers (file-system, github, shell) inherit the user's local privileges. Always run the read-only `host-list-mcp-config` (or grab the .quarantined sidecar after) for forensic review BEFORE attaching the AI prevention policy. Pair with extras_host_group_action(add-hosts). Irreversible (config preserved as .quarantined).

scripts.title: Uninstall ComfyUI (Shadow-AI eviction)
scripts.intent: Evict ComfyUI: kill any python.exe / pythonw.exe whose CIM cmdline references ComfyUI's main.py / server.py, then sweep the install root. ComfyUI is not a packaged installer — operator clones / extracts the portable zip into a folder of their choice; supply install_root if the scan output named the path (typical), otherwise the script walks candidate locations across every user profile (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, %LOCALAPPDATA%, root-of-drive, plus Pinokio's comfy.git). Sweep removes the models/ subtree (multi-GB checkpoints — main data-egress surface). Operator should copy models/ before approving if preservation matters. Irreversible.

install_root.description: Optional explicit install root from the Shadow-AI scan output (e.g. C:\ComfyUI_windows_portable). When omitted, the script walks a candidate list of common locations across every user profile.

scripts.title: Reboot the host (Restart-Computer -Force)
scripts.intent: Force-reboot the host. Use post-IR to (a) finalize Phase 2 cleanup actions that returned `pending_reboot` paths — locked files scheduled for next-boot delete via MoveFileEx are only removed on reboot — and (b) honor any operator-initiated reboot request after the workflow completes. NOT a Phase 2 cleanup primitive in itself; the IR playbook surfaces it after Phase 4 release if pending-reboot paths exist or the operator asks. The agent's RTR session is severed by Restart-Computer but the command completes successfully on the host. Mirror of the patching catalog's win-reboot — duplicated here so the IR-context agent doesn't have to reach across catalogs.
